title: Events API: respect the rate limit, drop the redeliveries

ticket.subject: The events vendor threatens to ban our key
body: The clickstream vendor wrote to us: our loader hammers their API after a `429 Too Many Requests` instead of
waiting the `Retry-After` they send. One more time and they revoke the key.
Also, their delivery is *at least once*: the same event (same `event_id`) can show up twice, a few pages
apart, and our dashboards count it twice.
Please make `ingest.py` wait what `Retry-After` says before retrying, and keep **one row per event** in

acceptance.text: bronze.api_events holds every event exactly once.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n, count(DISTINCT event_id) AS ids FROM bronze.api_events
checks.fail: The table does not hold every event exactly once.

acceptance.text: The last run met 429 answers and waited Retry-After every time, and read every page.

checks.fail: Your last run did not finish cleanly.
The request log shows requests sent during a Retry-After window, or pages never read.

hints: On a 429, read `response.headers["Retry-After"]` (seconds), `time.sleep()` that long, then send the same request again.
A fixed short sleep (0.2 s) or retrying at once counts as ignoring Retry-After, even if it works in the end.
Duplicates share an `event_id`: `bronze.merge("api_events", rows, key="event_id")` keeps one, or dedupe in Python before writing.
